column1: # fda_unwired_modules.tsv -- ostler_fda modules that SHIP and are DORMANT.
# Read by scripts/verify_fda_modules_reachable.py, printed IN FULL on every run,
# and verified on every PR by .github/workflows/fda-reachable.yml.
# A row here is an ACKNOWLEDGEMENT, not a suppression. It says: this module is
# in the shipped payload, nothing calls it, we know, and here is the concrete
# thing that blocks wiring it. The dormant count is reported SEPARATELY from the
# reachable count and never folded into it, because a dormant bucket that reads
# as a pass is exactly how a warn bucket collapses into green.
# RULES THE GATE ENFORCES (exit 2 if broken -- a malformed register is CANNOT
# RUN, never a quiet pass):
#   * status must be literally DORMANT. There is no other accepted value, and
#     there is deliberately NO blanket "ignore unreachable" switch: an
#     acknowledgement is per-module or it is not an acknowledgement.
#   * module must be a literal module name. Globs and wildcards are REFUSED --
#     one '*' would silently acknowledge every future orphan.
#   * blocked_by must be a real reason. Empty, '-', 'TBD', 'n/a' and friends
#     are refused. A row without a reason is a suppression wearing a reason's
#     clothes.
# A row is a named, dated debt, not permission to leave it dark. The gate fails
# the moment an UNREGISTERED orphan appears, and separately reports rows that
# are no longer orphans so a wired module cannot leave a stale row behind.
# columns: module<TAB>status<TAB>blocked_by<TAB>note

column3: BLOCKED ON THE HOUSEHOLD SPLIT: main() refuses to write unless a household-split marker exists (default ~/.ostler/household-split.done, override OSTLER_HOUSEHOLD_SPLIT_MARKER) and NOTHING in this repo creates that marker. Whoever ships the household split: WIRE THIS PASS AS PART OF THAT WORK. This row is here so you find it waiting rather than discovering a dark module a third time.
column4: v1018-D658/D659. Elects one displayName per person and demotes the rest to alternateName; deletes kinship words outright. Merged, tested by tests/test_name_repair.sh, gated by name-repair.yml, and PRESENT in the shipped v1.0.26 DMG -- verified byte-identical to main under OstlerInstaller.app/Contents/Resources/ostler_fda/. Kept deliberately rather than deleted: it is correct, it carries its own tests, and it is needed the moment the split lands. Measured 2026-08-15 against the SHIPPED copy with a stub graph and five synthetic nodes: --apply without the marker exits 2 and writes nothing; with the marker it applies three updates. Passing --households-already-split from install.sh would assert an environmental fact nobody measured, on a pass that deletes names with no undo. The intended trigger is UNRECORDED -- neither the module, its test nor its workflow says once, scheduled or on demand, and the docstring shows manual CLI use only.

column1: repair_role_address_people
column3: NO CALLER WAS EVER WRITTEN: unlike the row above this module has NO unmet precondition in its own code -- it is dry-run by default with --apply to write, and its safety predicates stand on their own. It is dormant purely because nothing ever invoked it. It is NOT blocked on the household split, and must not be wired on the strength of that row. || 2026-09-05, TNM: ITS SAFETY PREDICATES DO NOT STAND ON THEIR OWN WHILE A MERGE CAN TEAR, AND THAT SENTENCE ABOVE IS NOW WRONG. The module deletes a Person wholesale (DELETE WHERE { <uri> ?p ?o } at repair_role_address_people.py:264) and its own docstring says what keeps a real person safe: 'a node with identifiers, or one that anything points at, is never touched'. Its four criteria are is-a-Person, a role/bulk email, ZERO hasIdentifier, and nothing referencing it as an object. AN INTERRUPTED MERGE MANUFACTURES THREE OF THE FOUR. identity_resolver merge_persons is eight separate SPARQL updates: step 1 moves the identifiers (so ZERO remain), steps 2-3 move facts and attendee links (so nothing points at it), and step 7 -- which deletes the discard's rdf:type -- never runs if the process died first. install.sh SIGKILLs that resolver at the 300s dedupe budget and kill -9 cannot be trapped. So a node stranded mid-merge is STILL a Person, has ZERO identifiers and is referenced by nothing: it reads as a notification-sender to this module and is deleted wholesale, taking a real contact and the evidence of the tearing in one pass. 'Zero identifiers means never had any' is the assumption, and a rehoming falsifies it. DO NOT WIRE THIS until merge_persons writes its mergedInto tombstone BEFORE moving identifiers, at which point an interrupted merge is self-describing and this module's criteria are sound again. Measured from source, not the box: 0 keep_uri!=discard_uri guards in the module, 0 wholesale subject deletes in identity_resolver, and this is the only wholesale Person delete in vendor/.
column4: Deletes Person nodes that are a notification sender rather than a person, repairing over-merges that pwg_ingest.is_role_identifier now prevents at write time. Found by the same census that found the row above, which is the point of counting rather than remembering. Reachability is ALL that was established here: it has not been reviewed for correctness, ordering or blast radius, so treat wiring it as new work needing its own measurement.

column1: repair_overmerged_contact_cards
column3: NO CALLER YET, AND DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED IN THIS PR. Two concrete blocks. (1) The only sensible trigger is install.sh's contacts phase, and install.sh is ORM/Archie's ACTIVE lane cutting v1.0.39 -- editing it here would collide with a live cut. The handover anchors are in the PR that added this module. (2) MORE IMPORTANTLY, this repairs only the subset it can PROVE: measured on the live v1.0.38 box 2026-08-22 it repairs 30 of 128 over-merged nodes and leaves 98 untouched by design. Auto-running a partial repair on every customer graph is a product call about the other 98 that nobody has made yet, and the module is explicitly built to be run and reviewed rather than fired blind.
column4: Task #659. Un-merges Person nodes carrying 2+ distinct icloud_contact_uid -- RULE 2 of the ratified dedupe ruleset, violated 128 times on one real box (263 Contacts cards collapsed, 135 people with no node of their own; control 2259 icloud identifiers). identity_resolver RULE 2 stops NEW ones; this repairs the graph already written. Complements repair_role_address_people (row above), which deletes identifier-less robot nodes -- this one NEVER deletes a Person node, because these nodes carry real identifiers, attributes and inbound edges. Dry-run by default, --apply to write, --undo <movelog> to reverse; refuses to run at all if the icloud_contact_uid control is zero. PROVEN ON THE LIVE BOX 2026-08-22, both directions: 128 nodes/263 cards -> 99/204 on --apply, back to 128/263 on --undo, total triples 248082 -> 248065 -> 248082 exactly, and the 2259 control never moved so no card was destroyed. Tests: tests/test_repair_overmerged_contact_cards.py, 27 limbs incl. an anti-vacuity fixture check and 10 killed mutants.
